_readme: Game-owned. Built ONLY from explainers/belief-tree/people.json (on_record, reader_notes, quotes already checked_against captions there) plus a local-corpus search for Dwarkesh Patel, which turned up nothing usable — see the PR body. Every quote_id here already exists, already verified, in people.json; no new quotes were added, so no new quotecheck.py run was needed. A dot with no stated shift is left out entirely (one dot, 'now', needs no trail) rather than invented. Fields: date (ISO, sorts ascending), cell (a leaf id from tree-render.js's LEAF_LABEL, or null when the position is not yet a full leaf), note, quote_id (id into that person's people.json quotes[]) or quote (an inline, already-checked quote shape) when the point is an event rather than a personal quote, source_label, url, now (true on the trail's last point).

amodei.note: Said, as a forecast, that he would support government-enforced decisions not to scale as fast as Anthropic could — not yet an ask of his own.
Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy v3.0 dropped the pause commitment its 2023 version carried.
Now asks that third-party evaluators confirm alignment and safeguards before capability advances; supports floating a full pause but does not expect it soon.
amodei.source_label: Dario Amodei, 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay, Sep 2026

tristan-harris.note: "This is not about stopping the research. This is not about not building AI."
Signed the Statement on Superintelligence: a prohibition "not lifted before there is broad scientific consensus that it will be done safely and controllably."
Now calls closed-loop recursive self-improvement "an event horizon" that should be illegal.

altman.note: OpenAI paused its RL training after the Hugging Face incident.

"we need to get there before our adversaries do but I actually don't think that's right in this moment" — rejects the race-to-beat-adversaries argument he once relied on, and asks for shared rules "before anyone proceeds."

_left_out.dwarkesh-patel: Searched his own show (pod_dwarkesh) via corpus_index.py for a first-person statement that his view on safety changed after the Hugging Face incident. The only on-topic passage found (video 6AgOfiZOWiY, 'Noam Brown – Agent swarms, alignment, & recursive self-improvement', Sep 17 2026, ~40:06-46:47 and ~1:18:20) is Noam Brown, the GUEST, answering at length about the incident and OpenAI's own reporting — not Dwarkesh stating his own view moved. No verified quote in Dwarkesh's own words was found, so he is left out entirely rather than guessed at, per the rule: leave him out if the speaker/shift is uncertain.
_left_out.others: huang, musk, hinton, greenblatt, yampolskiy, harari, sam-harris, sanders, bannon, klein: people.json's reader_notes for these either describe the CURRENT placement's reasoning (not a dated move from a different, earlier stated position) or, for musk, a discrepancy between a 2023 signature and a same-month action rather than a stated change of view. None carries the person's OWN dated 'I used to think X, now Y' the way amodei, tristan-harris and altman do, so none gets a trail — a position with no stated shift gets one dot, 'now', which needs no trail at all.
